function: Excluded (function): the learned KAN predicts RSRP or path loss from distance, frequency and heights (radio map prediction), p. 4; it solves none of the seven areas.
notes: Exclusion code function. The paper is a research article with a trained model (RadioKAN, Kolmogorov-Arnold network), so source_type, survey and no_learning do not apply. The learned model does radio map prediction, a large-scale propagation regression, not a physical-layer function of the seven areas. Evidence: p. 1 abstract 'propose a new interpretable radio map prediction framework'; p. 4 'the path loss P (dBm) at the reception point is taken as the output'; p. 6 'Lpred uses the Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss function to approximate the RSRP values'; p. 9 'the RSRP is used as output'. Inputs are distance, frequency, antenna and building heights, LOS flag, or receiver position (pp. 4, 9). ISAC appears only as motivation (p. 1 'a key component of Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems'); the paper designs no ISAC beams, waveforms or resources, so area 5 does not apply. No MIMO detection, channel estimation or feedback of CSI, beamforming or RIS, OTFS, NTN link control or over-the-air federated learning is treated, and the system has no MIMO or RIS. Borderline for the reviewer: radio map prediction could be read as large-scale channel prediction (area 2), but the output is received power over a map for network planning, closer to the excluded spectrum prediction (p. 14 refs [24], [25], [27] are spectrum map and spectrum cartography works). PDF checked: the first page holds the title 'KAN-Based Interpretable Radio Map Prediction Framework With Symbolic Data Fusion' and the DOI 10.1109/TCCN.2025.3603700, which match the DOI of the work.
